method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two connected triangles: A, B, C lie on one straight line, and E, D, B lie on another straight line, with triangle ABE on the left and triangle DBC on the right. From the text, use ∠A = 60°, ∠E = 40°, and ∠C = 30°. In triangle ABE, compute ∠ABE = 180° - 60° - 40° = 80°. Since AB and BC are opposite rays on the same straight line, and BE and BD are the same line, ∠DBC is supplementary to ∠ABE, so ∠DBC = 100°. Then in triangle DBC, ∠BDC = 180° - 100° - 30° = 50°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing D on line EB and A, B, C on a straight baseline. From the text, ∠A = 60° and ∠E = 40° in triangle ABE, so ∠ABE = 80°. Because D lies on BE and A lies on the extension of CB through B, the angle ∠ABD is an exterior angle of triangle BDC at B. Thus the exterior angle theorem gives ∠ABD = ∠BCD + ∠BDC. Substitute ∠ABD = 80° and ∠BCD = 30°, giving ∠BDC = 80° - 30° = 50°.
